Synopsis:
This owlbear has been captured by the goblins. It is a cub and has been tormented by the goblins. In this dialog the player can reassure it, guide it to safety, or encourage it to attack the goblins. If the player has convinced his captors to release him, they can invite him to their camp. The owlbear refuses - but will show up later on his own.

Cluster Contexts:
- GOB_ChickenChase_Owlbear.json: You are in a raucous goblin camp where a young owlbear cub has been captured, teased and tormented; its mother has been taken or killed off‑screen, leaving the cub frightened and/or furious. The scene is public—other goblins (and possibly captives like Volo), taunting commentators, and party games are watching—so your words can either calm the cub, stoke its rage to attack the goblins, or coax it to follow you to safety. In some playthroughs you may already have been involved in goblin sabotage (poisoned beer or similar), which colors how the goblins interact with you and whether they’ll release the cub. If convinced to let it go, the cub initially refuses an invitation to the goblin camp but may later reappear of its own accord.

If the player helps him, he becomes excited and runs off to hunt. In the next night, he returns with a dead bird.The owlbear has appeared in camp for a second night.  The player has previously spared the cub after killing its mother, and saved it from a cruel game run by the goblins in their camp.
He reacts much more suspiciously of the player if they antagonised him in their first encounter.

context: You're in a rowdy goblin camp where a young owlbear cub has been captured, taunted and tormented; its mother has been taken or killed off‑screen and other goblins (and possibly captives) are watching the scene. In the exchange the player can try to calm and reassure the feral cub, coax it to follow them to safety, or stoke its fury to attack the goblins; if the player persuades the goblins to release it, the cub will still refuse an offer to join the goblin camp. If helped in this encounter, the cub becomes a permanent camp follower and will reappear the next night (bringing a dead bird). The cub speaks in short, staccato bursts, is slightly injured and distrustful (sometimes exaggerating wounds), and will react worse if the player antagonised it in an earlier meeting; prior player actions toward the goblins (sabotage, etc.) can also affect whether the goblins cooperate.
